value.rationale: The first negative Taylor coefficient is a mathematically natural finite detection complexity of failure of complete Pick interpolation under Schur multiplication. Its exact b^(-1/a) growth and parity-scaled limit exhibit singular sensitivity of the global property despite arbitrarily long positive finite tests. The new boundary branch-point mechanism contrasts meaningfully with known small finite-pole perturbations whose CNP property persists. No downstream theorem is required for value.
